name: Vienna Bread
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: In three tablespoons milk and water dissolve the yeast thoroughly and add to remaining milk and water.
Add salt and sufficient flour (warmed) to make a light dough (about four cups).
Turn out and knead until thoroughly smooth and does not stick to the hands.
Put in a greased basin, cover, and stand in a warm place to rise, for three hours.
When risen, turn out and cut into small rolls, knead each roll a little and put in a greased tin.
Grease over tops with melted butter, cover and stand in a warm place till twice their original size.
Grease again and bake in a hot oven.

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. In three tablespoons milk and water dissolve the yeast thoroughly and add to remaining milk and water.
2. Add salt and sufficient flour (warmed) to make a light dough (about four cups).
3. Turn out and knead until thoroughly smooth and does not stick to the hands.
4. Put in a greased basin, cover, and stand in a warm place to rise, for three hours.
5. When risen, turn out and cut into small rolls, knead each roll a little and put in a greased tin.
6. Grease over tops with melted butter, cover and stand in a warm place till twice their original size.
7. Grease again and bake in a hot oven.
